backlog task edit APRV-303 --append-notes "## Diagnosis (2026-09-07, before any fix)

**Root cause: the post-execution reading is written against a payload shape Claude Code never sends.**

\`readReportedOutcome\` in \`src/cli/hook.ts\` reads the outcome off \`tool_response.type\`, accepting exactly \`text\`, \`base64\` and \`error\`, per the contract pinned in docs/claude-code-hook.md. Claude Code's PostToolUse event does not carry a content block there. It carries the TOOL'S OWN output object, verbatim. From the shipped type declarations in \`@anthropic-ai/claude-code/sdk-tools.d.ts\`:

- \`BashOutput\` (Bash): \`stdout\`, \`stderr\`, \`interrupted\`, \`isImage?\`, \`returnCodeInterpretation?\`, ... and NO \`type\` field.
- \`FileEditOutput\` (Edit, MultiEdit): \`filePath\`, \`oldString\`, \`newString\`, \`originalFile\`, \`structuredPatch\`, \`userModified\`, \`replaceAll\`. No \`type\` field.
- \`FileWriteOutput\` (Write): has \`type\`, whose values are \`create\` and \`update\`, neither of which is one of the three pinned readings.
- \`NotebookEditOutput\` (NotebookEdit): no \`type\`; it carries an optional \`error\` string instead.

So for every gated tool the reading falls through to the unreadable arm, prints \`post-tool-unreadable-outcome\` on stderr, and appends nothing. That is the whole of the 22052 unreported starts.

**Why the few that landed are all failures.** The hook's other reading is the event name: \`hook_event_name === \"PostToolUseFailure\"\` is a failure with no further inspection. \`PostToolUseFailure\` is a real Claude Code event and it is registered in the primary \`.claude/settings.json\` alongside PostToolUse; its input schema (read out of the shipped binary's own zod definitions) is \`{hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_use_id, error, is_interrupt?, duration_ms?}\`, with NO \`tool_response\` at all. PostToolUse's is \`{hook_event_name, tool_name, tool_input, tool_response, tool_use_id, duration_ms?}\`. Claude Code fires exactly one of the two: PostToolUse when the call succeeded, PostToolUseFailure when it did not.

The counterpart therefore reads failures perfectly and successes never. Measured on the primary log: of the reports that carry \`reported_by: post-tool-use\`, the \`agent:claude-code\` actor has 9 \`execution.failed\` and 0 \`execution.completed\`. Zero completions have ever been reported by this adapter. The loop streak of amended SPEC.md §10.2 is a ratchet: it can only increment, so every long session eventually reaches three and stays escalated, on the session scope and then on the actor scope, forever. Both standing escalations on this log are that.

**Which branch swallowed it, exactly.** \`runPostToolUse\` -> \`readReportedOutcome\` returns \`{ok:false}\` because \`response[\"type\"]\` is \`undefined\` (Bash, Edit, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit) or \`\"create\"\`/\`\"update\"\` (Write). \`finishHarnessExecution\` is never reached, so nothing is refused and nothing is appended. The stderr line is correct and machine-readable; it was simply never read by anybody, and \`approval status\`'s coverage row is informational by design, so the flood produced no failing check anywhere.

**Why the tests did not catch it.** Every PostToolUse case in \`tests/cli-hook.test.ts\` constructs \`tool_response: {type: \"text\"}\` or \`{type: \"error\"}\`. The suite pinned the documented contract against itself; no fixture ever carried a payload Claude Code actually emits.

**The second, separate half (AC #2): the floor predicate is skipped on the file-tool path.**

\`describeToolCall\` calls \`fileToolGate\`, which returns \`null\` whenever \`protectedPathClass(file, protected_paths)\` is \`null\`, that is for every ordinary source file. \`runHarnessHook\` then returns \`allow(\"<tool> is not a gated edit\")\` at the \`described.kind === \"allow\"\` early return, which sits ABOVE the \`harnessFloor\` lookup, above \`recordUnattended\`, and above everything that appends. So an ordinary Edit or Write under a tripped floor is not routed, is not counted, and records no \`execution.started\` that a completion could ever close. The shell path has no such hole: every Bash call is classified, floored, and charged a start. That is the disagreement the incident description recorded, an Edit-tool grant that did not clear the floor followed by eight further Edit calls allowed without routing. The granted Edit was a protected-path edit (\`policy.edit.spec\`), so it WAS gated and DID record a start; its completion was then swallowed by the reading bug above. The eight that followed were ordinary workspace edits, which the file-tool path never gates at all.

Global invariants in play: §11.1 invariant 1 (the report resolves its task and action keys from the verified log, never from the reporting event) and invariant 4 (a self-reported field may raise scrutiny and never lower it)."
